Why train here

How we run our courses, from your first enquiry to the next step.

  • Clear about each course

    We explain who a course is for, what it leads to and how it runs before you are asked to commit to anything.

  • Courses matched to the right base

    Each course page shows which of our bases run it, so you only see training you can actually take.

  • Practical and classroom routes

    Licence training is time in the vehicle. Driver CPC, ADR and Operator CPC are classroom courses, each with its own page.

  • A straightforward enquiry

    Tell us the course, your preferred base and how to reach you. An enquiry does not book a test or commit you to anything.

How training works

Four steps from first enquiry to the next stage. We confirm the length of your course when you enquire.

  1. Say what you want to drive

    Category C, Category C+E, Driver CPC, or one of the further courses. If you are not sure, tell us and we will help you choose.

  2. We check the licence you hold

    What you already hold decides the medical, theory and practical steps. We go through it with you before anything is arranged.

  3. Train at the right base

    Each course runs at the bases shown on its page, so you train where the course is offered.

  4. Prepare for the next step

    That may be a practical test or periodic training hours. We explain how booking works when you enquire.

Guides

Plain explanations of the licence, the medical and the test, with links to the relevant course pages.

  • Guide

    Which HGV licence do I need?

    The licence depends on the vehicle you want to drive, and on what you already hold. This guide separates the main goods-vehicle entitlements from Driver CPC. We confirm what applies to you when you enquire.

  • Guide

    Category C vs Category C+E

    Category C and Category C+E are both goods-vehicle entitlements. One is the rigid lorry. The other adds a trailer. They are trained and tested separately.

  • Guide

    How HGV training works

    HGV training is a sequence, not a single lesson. You say what you want to drive, the licence you already hold is checked, and the medical, theory and practical steps are planned around that. We confirm the length of your course when you enquire.

All guides

Questions

Which licence do I need?

Category C is the usual route onto a rigid lorry. Category C+E adds a trailer. Driver CPC is the professional qualification, not a vehicle category. The HGV training page compares them.

How much does training cost?

We quote for each course once we know the licence you hold and the training you need. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate costs where they apply.

Where does the training take place?

At our bases in Bristol, Taunton and Exeter. Not every course runs at every base, so each course page shows where it is offered. We send the site address and joining details when your course is agreed.

What is the difference between Category C and Category C+E?

Category C is the rigid lorry entitlement. Category C+E adds a trailer, for articulated lorries and drawbar outfits. C+E training normally follows Category C.

Do I need a medical?

A medical report is normally required before a lorry practical test. Whether it applies to you depends on the entitlement and on current DVLA rules.

What happens after I enquire?

You tell us the course you want, your preferred base and how to contact you. We reply using that method to talk through the licence you hold and the next step. The form does not book a test.
